title: File Storage (EFS / Azure Files)
definition: A cloud storage service that mimics traditional network-attached storage (NAS). It allows multiple cloud servers to mount the exact same file system simultaneously over the network.
simpleExplanation: A shared network drive for your cloud servers. Server A writes a log file into the drive, and Server B can instantly open and read that exact same file like it was on its own hard drive.
realWorldExample: AWS EFS, Azure Files, GCP Filestore. A legacy CMS application requires multiple web servers to share a single 'uploads' directory for user files. They mount an EFS drive to all the web servers simultaneously.

basic: Can multiple virtual machines connect to a File Storage drive at the exact same time?
intermediate: How does File Storage (EFS) differ from Block Storage (EBS) regarding multi-instance mounting?

answers.question: Multiple VMs at once?
answers.answer: Yes. This is the primary feature of File Storage (using protocols like NFS or SMB).

answers.question: EFS vs EBS mounting?
answers.answer: By default, Block Storage (EBS) can only be attached to ONE single Virtual Machine at a time. File Storage (EFS) can be simultaneously mounted to thousands of VMs across multiple Availability Zones.
